By consent, these writ petitions are taken up for final disposal.

2. The petitioners in W.P.Nos.24870 and 24871 of 2017, on an earlier occasion approached this Court by filing W.P.Nos.33918 of 2015 and 22704 of 2014, praying for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the Commissioner, Corporation of Chennai to consider their representation with regard to licence to run the bunk shops/kiosks and vide order dated 18.11.2015 and 21.08.2014 respectively

, this Court has directed the concerned respondents to consider and dispose of the petitioners' representation on its own merits and in accordance with law within a stipulated time and in the interregnum, directed to maintain Status Quo till the disposal of the above said representations.

3. The Ambattur Industrial Estate Manufacturers Association also filed W.P.No.5232 of 2014 against the Tamil Nadu Small Scale Industries Development Corporation, TANSIDCO, Guindy,
Chennai-32 and two others praying for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents to remove the encroachments caused by the petty shops run in kiosks, bunkers within the SIDCO Ambattur Industrial Estate Area and vide order dated 21.11.2016, this Court directed TANSIDCO to take action against any encroachment or bunk shops operating in accordance with law subject to any interdict which may be operating by reason of any Court order.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Small Scale Industries Development Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The fourth respondent, in compliance of the order dated 21.11.2016 made in W.P.No.5232 of 2014, has issued notices to the petitioners dated 03.03.2017 calling upon them to vacate the encroachment and remove the bunk shops or kiosks and all other belongings within 10 days from the date of receipt of the Krishnasamy vs The Special Commissioner on 18 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17303679/
2 notice/affixing the notice, failing which appropriate action will be taken to remove the encroachments.

The petitioners, in response to the said notice, had also submitted their reply/representation dated 10.03.2017 praying permission/licence to run the bunk shop for the reason that they are physically challenged/differently abled and they and their family are dependent upon the income derived from running the bunk shops and since it has not been disposed of, the petitioners came forward with these writ petitions.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners are also entitled to the benefit of the Street Vendors [Protection of Livelihood and Regulation] Act, 2014 and therefore, prays for appropriate orders.

entities.text: Street Vendors [Protection of Livelihood and Regulation] Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, Mr.V.P.Senguttuvel, learned counsel appearing for the respondents 2 to 4 has drawn the attention of this Court to the photographs available at Page No.33 of the typed set of documents and would submit that even from the photographs it appears that the bunk shops are of very recent origin and the petitioners have put up notice which would indicate as if their earlier writ petitions are pending and continue to run the bunk shops or kiosks in an unauthorized and illegal manner and prays for dismissal of these writ petitions with costs.

6. Heard the submissions of Mr.A.N.Thambidurai, learned Special Government Pleader who accepts notice on behalf of the first respondent and Mr.A.Nagarajan, learned counsel who accepts notice on behalf of the respondents 5 to 7 also.
7.
This Court has considered the rival submissions and also perused the entire materials placed before it.

8. Though the petitioners pray for larger relief, this Court, in the light of the above facts and circumstances and without going into the merits of the claim projected by the petitioners, permits the petitioners to respond to the notices dated 03.03.2017 sent by the fourth respondent in the form of reply/representation by enclosing the necessary and authenticated documents along with a copy of this order, within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and the fourth respondent, upon receipt of the same, is directed to consider the said reply/representation on merits and pass orders in accordance with law within a period of two weeks thereafter and communicate the decision taken, to the petitioners and till such time, the respondents shall defer further proceedings in terms of the notice dated 03.03.2017.

It is also made clear that till the disposal of the representation by the fourth respondent, the petitioners shall not create any third party rights in respect of the bunk shops or kiosks in question and shall not commit any further encroachment and maintain the place in clean and hygienic manner and fully comply with Food Safety Standards Authority of India [FSSAI] norms.

entities.text: Food Safety Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 9. These writ petitions are disposed of with the above directions.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
